message: PH-3.1 requires every existing plan to satisfy all nine sections, but active/completed plans fail and the write scope excludes plans/**; authorize the failing plan files or revise the shipped-plan acceptance criterion.

notes: The rule was wrong, not the scope. Three of the failing files are not plans at all — plans/README.md is a readme, assumptions.md and deferrals.md are ledgers — so a check that globs plans/**/*.md is checking the wrong set. And the archived plans genuinely fail: FORGE-INIT-1 misses eight sections, harness-v2-wedge five. They shipped under an earlier contract, and rewriting them to satisfy a rule invented afterwards would falsify the record. PH-3.1 now binds at SAVE time to plan documents only, archived plans are explicitly left alone, and write_scope stays as it was. Re-recorded; resume.

message: PH-3.2 brief says the leaf task is active and .factory/run.json says phase implementing, but ./forge next reports PH-3 ready for PR gate; stage authority is contradictory before scoped implementation begins.

PH-3.3 requires deleting render_linear_task_graph.py with zero repo-wide references, but factory/scripts/check_factory_scaffold.py and docs/FACTORY.md still reference it and are outside the task write scope; the scope or acceptance criteria must be revised.

notes: You read it correctly and stage authority wins: .factory/stages.json says PH-3.3 is the active leaf, and that is the truth. ./forge next is wrong here for a real reason — phase.py only consults stage state when tests.json has no automated record, and this worktree contains FORGE-UPG-1's tests.json, verify.json, reviews/ and outcome.json, inherited by merging origin/main. Foreign evidence, not PH-3's. That is being handled at the story level and is not yours to fix. Proceed with PH-3.3's scoped work: retire authored build_waves from decomposer.md and griller.md, delete render_linear_task_graph.py in the same change, keep the schema field optional so .factory/history artifacts still parse.

Correct on both counts, and I had already hit one of them before seeing this signal. check_factory_scaffold.py listed the renderer as REQUIRED scaffold, so deleting it made the scaffold check fail outright — the deletion is not atomic until every reference goes with it, which is the same writer/reader rule pointing a third way. docs/FACTORY.md also advertised the command. PH-3.3's write scope now includes both files, re-recorded and ledgered; both references are gone and check_factory_scaffold reports OK. Resume.

message: PH-3.3 must stop anything authoring build_waves, but .codex/agents/docs-decomposer.toml still lists build_waves in the active decomposer output contract and is outside the task write scope; add that path to scope or narrow the acceptance criterion explicitly.

notes: Correct, and factory/prompts/decomposer.md was not the only place the decomposer is told what to emit — .codex/agents/docs-decomposer.toml carried the same output contract. An agent still authoring a field whose only reader was deleted is exactly the orphan this task exists to close, so the acceptance criterion stands and the scope was wrong. Path added to write_scope, re-recorded and ledgered; build_waves now appears in no prompt, no agent contract and no doc. Resume.
